questions.question: How are you assessed under SPI?

options.A: One final assessment at the end of the course.
options.C: Four checkpoints: Classroom Quizzes, Module Quizzes, Skill Assessments, and Final Skill Assessment.
options.D: Weekly tests with no final assessment.

explanation: SPI tracks your progress through Classroom Quizzes, Module Quizzes, Skill Assessments, and the Final Skill Assessment. Each checkpoint contributes to your overall SPI score.

questions.question: Which assessment carries the highest weightage?
explanation: The Final Skill Assessment carries 50%. Skill Assessments carry 25%, Module Quizzes 15% and Classroom Quizzes 10%.
Every checkpoint counts, so start preparing from day one.

questions.question: Scoring below what % puts a course in Skill Debt?
explanation: Below 50% is an F and earns 0 points. Being absent (Ab) also earns 0. Either one becomes a Skill Debt.
Scores of 50% and above earn 6 to 10 points, and you need at least 50% in every assessment to get SPI.

questions.question: Which of the following is required to earn your SPI?

options.A: Minimum 60% attendance and an attempt at the Final Skill Assessment.
options.B: A high final score that compensates for missed Classroom quizzes and low attendance.
options.C: Minimum 80% attendance, 100% completion of all classroom quizzes, Module quizzes and skill assessments, a mandatory Final Skill Assessment, and no malpractice cases.
options.D: Minimum 80% attendance alone; assessments are optional.

explanation: To earn SPI, you must maintain at least 80% attendance, complete all required assessments, take the mandatory Final Skill Assessment, and have no malpractice cases. All requirements must be met.

questions.question: Minimum attendance needed to earn SPI?
explanation: You need at least 80% attendance. If it drops below that, Recovery Mode applies.

questions.question: Your attendance drops below 80%. What happens?

options.B: Nothing, if you pass the exams
options.D: You are removed from the course

explanation: You must attend assigned recovery classes to reach 80% again. Watching recordings doesn't undo an absence.
If you skip recovery classes, you can't sit the assessment and the course becomes a Skill Debt. For a genuine medical or emergency absence, submit proof within 5 days.

questions.question: Which assessments must you take part in to earn SPI?
explanation: Classroom Quizzes, Module Quizzes, Skill Assessments and the Final Skill Assessment all need full participation. Any malpractice case also makes you ineligible.

questions.question: With an active Skill Debt, what is put on hold?
explanation: Even one Skill Debt blocks MINT, BRAVE, GRIT, placements, internships and co-curricular support until it is cleared.
Clear it within the next cycle, or face a review.

questions.question: What should you maintain to achieve a good SPI score?
explanation: Maintain an average above 80% in Skill Assessments, CQs, and MQs to achieve a good SPI score.

questions.question: What happens if you are caught cheating in an exam?
explanation: NIAT has zero tolerance. The course result is reset to fail, with no retake that skill cycle.
You also lose any official position or title and are excluded from external PR activities. Plagiarism, fabricating data and unauthorised collaboration count too.
